ESV.1: Concerning the Ammonites. Thus says the LORD: “Has Israel no sons? Has he no heir? Why then has Milcom  dispossessed Gad, and his people settled in its cities?
ESV.2: Therefore, behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will cause the battle cry to be heard against Rabbah of the Ammonites; it shall become a desolate mound, and its villages shall be burned with fire; then Israel shall dispossess those who dispossessed him, says the LORD.
ESV.3: “Wail, O Heshbon, for Ai is laid waste! Cry out, O daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth, lament, and run to and fro among the hedges! For Milcom shall go into exile, with his priests and his officials.
ESV.4: Why do you boast of your valleys,  O faithless daughter, who trusted in her treasures, saying, ‘Who will come against me?’
ESV.5: Behold, I will bring terror upon you, declares the Lord GOD of hosts, from all who are around you, and you shall be driven out, every man straight before him, with none to gather the fugitives.
ESV.6: “But afterward I will restore the fortunes of the Ammonites, declares the LORD.”
ESV.7: Concerning Edom. Thus says the LORD of hosts: “Is wisdom no more in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom vanished?
ESV.8: Flee, turn back, dwell in the depths, O inhabitants of Dedan! For I will bring the calamity of Esau upon him, the time when I punish him.
ESV.9: If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings? If thieves came by night, would they not destroy only enough for themselves?
ESV.10: But I have stripped Esau bare; I have uncovered his hiding places, and he is not able to conceal himself. His children are destroyed, and his brothers, and his neighbors; and he is no more.
ESV.11: Leave your fatherless children; I will keep them alive; and let your widows trust in me.”
ESV.12: For thus says the LORD: “If those who did not deserve to drink the cup must drink it, will you go unpunished? You shall not go unpunished, but you must drink.
ESV.13: For I have sworn by myself, declares the LORD, that Bozrah shall become a horror, a taunt, a waste, and a curse, and all her cities shall be perpetual wastes.”
ESV.14: I have heard a message from the LORD, and an envoy has been sent among the nations: “Gather yourselves together and come against her, and rise up for battle!
ESV.15: For behold, I will make you small among the nations, despised among mankind.
ESV.16: The horror you inspire has deceived you, and the pride of your heart, you who live in the clefts of the rock,  who hold the height of the hill. Though you make your nest as high as the eagle's, I will bring you down from there, declares the LORD.
ESV.17: “Edom shall become a horror. Everyone who passes by it will be horrified and will hiss because of all its disasters.
ESV.18: As when Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighboring cities were overthrown, says the LORD, no man shall dwell there, no man shall sojourn in her.
ESV.19: Behold, like a lion coming up from the jungle of the Jordan against a perennial pasture, I will suddenly make him  run away from her. And I will appoint over her whomever I choose. For who is like me? Who will summon me? What shepherd can stand before me?
ESV.20: Therefore hear the plan that the LORD has made against Edom and the purposes that he has formed against the inhabitants of Teman: Even the little ones of the flock shall be dragged away. Surely their fold shall be appalled at their fate.
ESV.21: At the sound of their fall the earth shall tremble; the sound of their cry shall be heard at the Red Sea.
ESV.22: Behold, one shall mount up and fly swiftly like an eagle and spread his wings against Bozrah, and the heart of the warriors of Edom shall be in that day like the heart of a woman in her birth pains.”
ESV.23: Concerning Damascus: “Hamath and Arpad are confounded, for they have heard bad news; they melt in fear, they are troubled like the sea that cannot be quiet.
ESV.24: Damascus has become feeble, she turned to flee, and panic seized her; anguish and sorrows have taken hold of her, as of a woman in labor.
ESV.25: How is the famous city not forsaken, the city of my joy?
ESV.26: Therefore her young men shall fall in her squares, and all her soldiers shall be destroyed in that day, declares the LORD of hosts.
ESV.27: And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it shall devour the strongholds of Ben-hadad.”
ESV.28: Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck down. Thus says the LORD: “Rise up, advance against Kedar! Destroy the people of the east!
ESV.29: Their tents and their flocks shall be taken, their curtains and all their goods; their camels shall be led away from them, and men shall cry to them: ‘Terror on every side!’
ESV.30: Flee, wander far away, dwell in the depths, O inhabitants of Hazor! declares the LORD. For Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has made a plan against you and formed a purpose against you.
ESV.31: “Rise up, advance against a nation at ease, that dwells securely, declares the LORD, that has no gates or bars, that dwells alone.
ESV.32: Their camels shall become plunder, their herds of livestock a spoil. I will scatter to every wind those who cut the corners of their hair, and I will bring their calamity from every side of them, declares the LORD.
ESV.33: Hazor shall become a haunt of jackals, an everlasting waste; no man shall dwell there; no man shall sojourn in her.”
ESV.34: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah.
ESV.35: Thus says the LORD of hosts: “Behold, I will break the bow of Elam, the mainstay of their might.
ESV.36: And I will bring upon Elam the four winds from the four quarters of heaven. And I will scatter them to all those winds, and there shall be no nation to which those driven out of Elam shall not come.
ESV.37: I will terrify Elam before their enemies and before those who seek their life. I will bring disaster upon them, my fierce anger, declares the LORD. I will send the sword after them, until I have consumed them,
ESV.38: and I will set my throne in Elam and destroy their king and officials, declares the LORD.
ESV.39: “But in the latter days I will restore the fortunes of Elam, declares the LORD.”

NLT.1:
This message was given concerning the Ammonites. This is what the LORD says: “Are there no descendants of Israel
to inherit the land of Gad?
Why are you, who worship Molech,
living in its towns?
NLT.2:
In the days to come,” says the LORD,
“I will sound the battle cry against your city of Rabbah.
It will become a desolate heap of ruins,
and the neighboring towns will be burned.
Then Israel will take back the land
you took from her,” says the LORD.
NLT.3:
“Cry out, O Heshbon,
for the town of Ai is destroyed.
Weep, O people of Rabbah!
Put on your clothes of mourning.
Weep and wail, hiding in the hedges,
for your god Molech, with his priests and officials,
will be hauled off to distant lands.
NLT.4:
You are proud of your fertile valleys,
but they will soon be ruined.
You trusted in your wealth,
you rebellious daughter,
and thought no one could ever harm you.
NLT.5:
But look! I will bring terror upon you,”
says the Lord, the LORD of Heaven’s Armies.
“Your neighbors will chase you from your land,
and no one will help your exiles as they flee.
NLT.6:
But I will restore the fortunes of the Ammonites
in days to come.
I, the LORD, have spoken.”
NLT.7:
This message was given concerning Edom. This is what the LORD of Heaven’s Armies says: “Is there no wisdom in Teman?
Is no one left to give wise counsel?
NLT.8:
Turn and flee!
Hide in deep caves, you people of Dedan!
For when I bring disaster on Edom,
I will punish you, too!
NLT.9:
Those who harvest grapes
always leave a few for the poor.
If thieves came at night,
they would not take everything.
NLT.10:
But I will strip bare the land of Edom,
and there will be no place left to hide.
Its children, its brothers, and its neighbors
will all be destroyed,
and Edom itself will be no more.
NLT.11:
But I will protect the orphans who remain among you.
Your widows, too, can depend on me for help.”
NLT.12: And this is what the LORD says: “If the innocent must suffer, how much more must you! You will not go unpunished! You must drink this cup of judgment!
NLT.13: For I have sworn by my own name,” says the LORD, “that Bozrah will become an object of horror and a heap of ruins; it will be mocked and cursed. All its towns and villages will be desolate forever.”
NLT.14:
I have heard a message from the LORD
that an ambassador was sent to the nations to say,
“Form a coalition against Edom,
and prepare for battle!”
NLT.15:
The LORD says to Edom,
“I will cut you down to size among the nations.
You will be despised by all.
NLT.16:
You have been deceived
by the fear you inspire in others
and by your own pride.
You live in a rock fortress
and control the mountain heights.
But even if you make your nest among the peaks with the eagles,
I will bring you crashing down,”
says the LORD.
NLT.17:
“Edom will be an object of horror.
All who pass by will be appalled
and will gasp at the destruction they see there.
NLT.18:
It will be like the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
and their neighboring towns,” says the LORD.
“No one will live there;
no one will inhabit it.
NLT.19:
I will come like a lion from the thickets of the Jordan,
leaping on the sheep in the pasture.
I will chase Edom from its land,
and I will appoint the leader of my choice.
For who is like me, and who can challenge me?
What ruler can oppose my will?”
NLT.20:
Listen to the LORD’s plans against Edom
and the people of Teman.
Even the little children will be dragged off like sheep,
and their homes will be destroyed.
NLT.21:
The earth will shake with the noise of Edom’s fall,
and its cry of despair will be heard all the way to the Red Sea.
NLT.22:
Look! The enemy swoops down like an eagle,
spreading his wings over Bozrah.
Even the mightiest warriors will be in anguish
like a woman in labor.
NLT.23:
This message was given concerning Damascus. This is what the LORD says: “The towns of Hamath and Arpad are struck with fear,
for they have heard the news of their destruction.
Their hearts are troubled
like a wild sea in a raging storm.
NLT.24:
Damascus has become feeble,
and all her people turn to flee.
Fear, anguish, and pain have gripped her
as they grip a woman in labor.
NLT.25:
That famous city, a city of joy,
will be forsaken!
NLT.26:
Her young men will fall in the streets and die.
Her soldiers will all be killed,”
says the LORD of Heaven’s Armies.
NLT.27:
“And I will set fire to the walls of Damascus
that will burn up the palaces of Ben-hadad.”
NLT.28:
This message was given concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which were attacked by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon. This is what the LORD says: “Advance against Kedar!
Destroy the warriors from the East!
NLT.29:
Their flocks and tents will be captured,
and their household goods and camels will be taken away.
Everywhere shouts of panic will be heard:
‘We are terrorized at every turn!’
NLT.30:
Run for your lives,” says the LORD.
“Hide yourselves in deep caves, you people of Hazor,
for King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon has plotted against you
and is preparing to destroy you.
NLT.31:
“Go up and attack that complacent nation,”
says the LORD.
“Its people live alone in the desert
without walls or gates.
NLT.32:
Their camels and other livestock will all be yours.
I will scatter to the winds these people
who live in remote places.
I will bring calamity upon them
from every direction,” says the LORD.
NLT.33:
“Hazor will be inhabited by jackals,
and it will be desolate forever.
No one will live there;
no one will inhabit it.”
NLT.34: This message concerning Elam came to the prophet Jeremiah from the LORD at the beginning of the reign of King Zedekiah of Judah.
NLT.35:
This is what the LORD of Heaven’s Armies says: “I will destroy the archers of Elam —
the best of their forces.
NLT.36:
I will bring enemies from all directions,
and I will scatter the people of Elam to the four winds.
They will be exiled to countries around the world.
NLT.37:
I myself will go with Elam’s enemies to shatter it.
In my fierce anger, I will bring great disaster
upon the people of Elam,” says the LORD.
“Their enemies will chase them with the sword
until I have destroyed them completely.
NLT.38:
I will set my throne in Elam,” says the LORD,
“and I will destroy its king and officials.
NLT.39:
But I will restore the fortunes of Elam
in days to come.
I, the LORD, have spoken!”

AMP.1:
Concerning the sons (descendants) of Ammon.
Thus says the LORD:
"Does Israel have no sons [to reclaim Gad from the Ammonites]?
Has he no heir?
Why then has Malcam taken possession of Gad
And [why do] his people live in the cities [of Gad]?
AMP.2:
"Therefore behold, the days are coming," says the LORD,
"When I will cause an alarm of war to be heard
Against Rabbah of the Ammonites;
And it [along with the high ground on which it stands] will become a desolate heap,
And its villages will be set on fire.
Then will Israel take possession of his possessors,"
Says the LORD.
AMP.3:
"Wail, O Heshbon, for Ai [in Ammon] has been destroyed!
Cry out, O daughters of Rabbah!
Wrap yourselves with sackcloth and lament (cry out in grief),
And rush back and forth inside the enclosures;
For Malcam [your powerless god] will go into exile
Together with his priests and his princes.
AMP.4:
"Why do you boast of your valleys?
Your valley is flowing away,
[O Ammon] rebellious and faithless daughter
Who trusts in her treasures, saying,
'Who will come against me?'
AMP.5:
"Behold, I am going to bring terror on you,"
Says the Lord GOD of hosts,
"From all who are around you;
And each of you will be driven out headlong,
And there will be no one to gather the fugitives together.
AMP.6:
"But afterward I will reverse
The captivity of the children of Ammon and restore their fortunes,"
Says the LORD.
AMP.7:
Concerning Edom.
Thus says the LORD of hosts,
"Is there no longer any wisdom in Teman?
Has good counsel vanished from the intelligent and prudent?
Has their wisdom decayed?
AMP.8:
"Flee, turn back, dwell in the depths [of the desert to escape the judgment of Edom],
O inhabitants of Dedan,
For I will bring the destruction of Esau (Edom) upon him
When I inspect and punish him.
AMP.9:
"If grape gatherers came to you,
Would they not leave some ungleaned grapes [on the vines]?
If thieves came by night,
Would they not destroy [only] what is enough [for them]?
AMP.10:
"But I have stripped Esau (Edom) bare;
I have uncovered his hiding places
And he cannot hide himself.
His descendants have been destroyed along with his brothers (relatives) and his neighbors;
And he is no more.
AMP.11:
"Leave your orphans behind; I will [do what is needed to] keep them alive.
And let [those who are] your widows trust and confide in Me."
AMP.12: For thus says the LORD, "Behold, those (Israel) who were not sentenced to drink the cup [of wrath] shall certainly drink it, and are you to remain unpunished? You will not be acquitted and go unpunished, but you will certainly drink [from the cup of wrath and judgment].
AMP.13: For I have sworn [an oath] by Myself," says the LORD, "that Bozrah will become an object of horror, a reproach, a ruin, and a curse; and all its cities will become perpetual ruins."
AMP.14:
I have heard a report from the LORD,
And a messenger has been sent to the nations, saying,
"Gather together and come against her,
And rise up for the battle."
AMP.15:
"For behold, [Edom] I have made you small among the nations
And despised among men.
AMP.16:
"As for Your terror,
The pride and arrogance of your heart have deceived you,
O you who live in the clefts of the rock (Sela also called Petra),
Who hold and occupy the height of the hill.
Though you make your nest as high as the eagle's,
I will bring you down from there," says the LORD.
AMP.17: "Edom will become an object of horror; everyone who goes by it will be astonished and shall hiss [scornfully] at all its plagues and disasters.
AMP.18: As [it was] in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah with their neighboring cities," says the LORD, "no man will live there, nor will a son of man dwell in it.
AMP.19: See, one will come like a lion from the thicket of the Jordan against the enduring habitation [of Edom] and its watered pastures; for in an instant I will make him (Edom) run from his land. I will appoint over him the one whom I choose. For who is like Me, and who will summon Me [into court] and prosecute Me [for this]? Who is the [earthly] shepherd who can stand [defiantly] before Me?"
AMP.20: Therefore hear the plan of the LORD which He has devised against Edom, and [hear] what He has purposed against the inhabitants of Teman: surely they will be dragged away, even the little ones of the flock; surely He will make their dwelling place desolate because of them.
AMP.21: The earth has quaked at the noise of their downfall. There is an outcry! The sound of its noise has been heard at the Red Sea.
AMP.22: Behold, He will mount up and fly swiftly like an eagle and spread His wings against [the city of] Bozrah; and in that day the heart of the mighty warriors of Edom will be like the heart of a woman in childbirth.
AMP.23:
Concerning Damascus [in Syria].
"Hamath and Arpad are perplexed and shamed,
For they have heard bad news;
They are disheartened;
Troubled and anxious like a [storm-tossed] sea
Which cannot be calmed.
AMP.24:
"Damascus has become helpless;
She has turned away to flee,
Terror (panic) has seized her;
Anguish and distress have gripped her
Like a woman in childbirth.
AMP.25:
"Why has the renowned city not been deserted,
The city of My joy!
AMP.26:
"Therefore, her young men will fall in her streets,
And all her men of war will be destroyed in that day," says the LORD of hosts.
AMP.27:
"I will set fire to the wall of Damascus,
And it will consume the palaces of Ben-hadad."
AMP.28:
Concerning Kedar and concerning the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated. Thus says the LORD,
"Arise, go up against Kedar
And destroy the men of the east.
AMP.29:
"They (the Babylonians) will take away their tents and their flocks;
They will carry off for themselves
Their tent curtains, all their goods and their camels,
And they will call out to one another, 'Terror on every side!'
AMP.30:
"Flee, run far away! Dwell in the depths [of the desert],
O inhabitants of Hazor," says the LORD,
"For Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has planned a course of action against you
And devised a scheme against you.
AMP.31:
"Arise [Nebuchadnezzar], go up against a nation which is at ease,
Which lives securely," says the LORD,
"A nation which has neither gates nor bars;
They dwell apart and alone.
AMP.32:
"Their camels will become plunder,
And their herds of cattle a spoil;
And I will scatter to all the [four] winds those who cut the corners of their hair [as evidence of their idolatry],
And I will bring their disaster from every side," says the LORD.
AMP.33:
"Hazor will become a haunt and dwelling place of jackals,
A desolation forever;
No one will live there,
Nor will a son of man reside in it."
AMP.34: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying:
AMP.35:
"Thus says the LORD of hosts,
'Behold (listen carefully), I am going to break the bow of Elam,
The finest [weapon] of their strength.
AMP.36:
'And I will bring upon Elam the four winds
From the four corners of heaven;
And I will scatter them toward all those winds,
And there will be no nation
To which the outcasts of Elam will not go.
AMP.37:
'So I will cause Elam to be shattered (dismayed) before their enemies
And before those who seek their lives;
And I will bring disaster on them,
Even My fierce anger,' says the LORD.
'And I will send the sword after them
Until I have consumed them.
AMP.38:
'Then I will set My throne [of judgment] in Elam
And I will destroy from there the king and princes,'
Says the LORD.
AMP.39:
'But it will be in the last days (the end of days)
That I will reverse the captivity and restore the fortunes of Elam,'"
Says the LORD.

Why do his people live in its towns?

declares the Lord,

and its surrounding villages will be set on fire.

those who drove her out,”

rush here and there inside the walls,

NRSVCE.13: For by myself I have sworn, says the LORD, that Bozrah shall become an object of horror and ridicule, a waste, and an object of cursing; and all her towns shall be perpetual wastes.
NRSVCE.14:
I have heard tidings from the LORD,
and a messenger has been sent among the nations:
“Gather yourselves together and come against her,
and rise up for battle!”
NRSVCE.15:
For I will make you least among the nations,
despised by humankind.
NRSVCE.16:
The terror you inspire
and the pride of your heart have deceived you,
you who live in the clefts of the rock,
who hold the height of the hill.
Although you make your nest as high as the eagle’s,
from there I will bring you down,
— says the LORD.
NRSVCE.17: Edom shall become an object of horror; everyone who passes by it will be horrified and will hiss because of all its disasters.
NRSVCE.18: As when Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors were overthrown, says the LORD, no one shall live there, nor shall anyone settle in it.
NRSVCE.19: Like a lion coming up from the thickets of the Jordan against a perennial pasture, I will suddenly chase Edom away from it; and I will appoint over it whomever I choose. For who is like me? Who can summon me? Who is the shepherd who can stand before me?
NRSVCE.20: Therefore hear the plan that the LORD has made against Edom and the purposes that he has formed against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely the little ones of the flock shall be dragged away; surely their fold shall be appalled at their fate.
NRSVCE.21: At the sound of their fall the earth shall tremble; the sound of their cry shall be heard at the Red Sea.
NRSVCE.22: Look, he shall mount up and swoop down like an eagle, and spread his wings against Bozrah, and the heart of the warriors of Edom in that day shall be like the heart of a woman in labor.
NRSVCE.23:
Concerning Damascus. Hamath and Arpad are confounded,
for they have heard bad news;
they melt in fear, they are troubled like the sea
that cannot be quiet.
NRSVCE.24:
Damascus has become feeble, she turned to flee,
and panic seized her;
anguish and sorrows have taken hold of her,
as of a woman in labor.
NRSVCE.25:
How the famous city is forsaken,
the joyful town!
NRSVCE.26:
Therefore her young men shall fall in her squares,
and all her soldiers shall be destroyed in that day,
— says the LORD of hosts.
NRSVCE.27:
And I will kindle a fire at the wall of Damascus,
and it shall devour the strongholds of Ben-hadad.
NRSVCE.28:
Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor that King Nebuchadrezzar of Babylon defeated. Thus says the LORD:
Rise up, advance against Kedar!
Destroy the people of the east!
NRSVCE.29:
Take their tents and their flocks,
their curtains and all their goods;
carry off their camels for yourselves,
and a cry shall go up: “Terror is all around!”
NRSVCE.30:
Flee, wander far away, hide in deep places,
O inhabitants of Hazor!
— says the LORD.
For King Nebuchadrezzar of Babylon
has made a plan against you
and formed a purpose against you.
NRSVCE.31:
Rise up, advance against a nation at ease,
that lives secure,
— says the LORD,
that has no gates or bars,
that lives alone.
NRSVCE.32:
Their camels shall become booty,
their herds of cattle a spoil.
I will scatter to every wind
those who have shaven temples,
and I will bring calamity
against them from every side,
— says the LORD.
NRSVCE.33:
Hazor shall become a lair of jackals,
an everlasting waste;
no one shall live there,
nor shall anyone settle in it.
NRSVCE.34: The word of the LORD that came to the prophet Jeremiah concerning Elam, at the beginning of the reign of King Zedekiah of Judah.
NRSVCE.35: Thus says the LORD of hosts: I am going to break the bow of Elam, the mainstay of their might;
NRSVCE.36: and I will bring upon Elam the four winds from the four quarters of heaven; and I will scatter them to all these winds, and there shall be no nation to which the exiles from Elam shall not come.
NRSVCE.37: I will terrify Elam before their enemies, and before those who seek their life; I will bring disaster upon them, my fierce anger, says the LORD. I will send the sword after them, until I have consumed them;
NRSVCE.38: and I will set my throne in Elam, and destroy their king and officials, says the LORD.
NRSVCE.39: But in the latter days I will restore the fortunes of Elam, says the LORD.

NET.1: The LORD spoke about the Ammonites. “Do you think there are not any people of the nation of Israel remaining? Do you think there are not any of them remaining to reinherit their land? Is that why you people who worship the god Milcom have taken possession of the territory of Gad and live in his cities?
NET.2: Because you did that, I, the LORD, affirm that a time is coming when I will make Rabbah, the capital city of Ammon, hear the sound of the battle cry. It will become a mound covered with ruins. Its villages will be burned to the ground. Then Israel will take back its land from those who took their land from them. I, the Lord, affirm it!
NET.3: Wail, you people in Heshbon, because Ai in Ammon is destroyed. Cry out in anguish, you people in the villages surrounding Rabbah. Put on sackcloth and cry out in mourning. Run about covered with gashes. For your god Milcom will go into exile along with his priests and officials.
NET.4: Why do you brag about your great power? Your power is ebbing away, you rebellious people of Ammon, who trust in your riches and say, ‘Who would dare to attack us?’
NET.5: I will bring terror on you from every side,” says the Lord GOD who rules over all. “You will be scattered in every direction. No one will gather the fugitives back together.
NET.6: Yet in days to come I will reverse Ammon’s ill fortune.” says the LORD.
NET.7: The LORD who rules over all spoke about Edom. “Is wisdom no longer to be found in Teman? Can Edom’s counselors not give her any good advice? Has all of their wisdom turned bad?
NET.8: Turn and flee! Take up refuge in remote places, you people who live in Dedan. For I will bring disaster on the descendants of Esau. I have decided it is time for me to punish them.
NET.9: If grape pickers came to pick your grapes, would they not leave a few grapes behind? If robbers came at night, would they not pillage only what they needed?
NET.10: But I will strip everything away from Esau’s descendants. I will uncover their hiding places so they cannot hide. Their children, relatives, and neighbors will all be destroyed. Not one of them will be left!
NET.11: Leave your orphans behind and I will keep them alive. Your widows too can depend on me.”
NET.12: For the LORD says, “If even those who did not deserve to drink from the cup of my wrath must drink from it, do you think you will go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, but must certainly drink from the cup of my wrath.
NET.13: For I solemnly swear,” says the LORD, “that Bozrah will become a pile of ruins. It will become an object of horror and ridicule, an example to be used in curses. All the towns around it will lie in ruins forever.”
NET.14: I said, “I have heard a message from the LORD. A messenger has been sent among the nations to say, ‘Gather your armies and march out against her! Prepare to do battle with her!’”
NET.15: The LORD says to Edom, “I will certainly make you small among nations. I will make you despised by all humankind.
NET.16: The terror you inspire in others and the arrogance of your heart have deceived you. You may make your home in the clefts of the rocks; you may occupy the highest places in the hills. But even if you made your home where the eagles nest, I would bring you down from there,” says the LORD.
NET.17: “Edom will become an object of horror. All who pass by it will be filled with horror; they will hiss out their scorn because of all the disasters that have happened to it.
NET.18: Edom will be destroyed like Sodom and Gomorrah and the towns that were around them. No one will live there. No human being will settle in it,” says the LORD.
NET.19: “A lion coming up from the thick undergrowth along the Jordan scatters the sheep in the pastureland around it. So too I will chase the Edomites off their land. Then I will appoint over it whomever I choose. For there is no one like me, and there is no one who can call me to account. There is no ruler who can stand up against me.
NET.20: So listen to what I, the LORD, have planned against Edom, what I intend to do to the people who live in Teman. Their little ones will be dragged off. I will completely destroy their land because of what they have done.
NET.21: The people of the earth will quake when they hear of their downfall. Their cries of anguish will be heard all the way to the Gulf of Aqaba.
NET.22: Look! Like an eagle with outspread wings, a nation will soar up and swoop down on Bozrah. At that time the soldiers of Edom will be as fearful as a woman in labor.”
NET.23: The LORD spoke about Damascus. “The people of Hamath and Arpad will be dismayed because they have heard bad news. Their courage will melt away because of worry. Their hearts will not be able to rest.
NET.24: The people of Damascus will lose heart and turn to flee. Panic will grip them. Pain and anguish will seize them like a woman in labor.
NET.25: How deserted will that once-famous city be, that city that was once filled with joy!
NET.26: For her young men will fall in her city squares. All her soldiers will be destroyed at that time,” says the LORD who rules over all.
NET.27: “I will set fire to the walls of Damascus; it will burn up the palaces of Ben Hadad.”
NET.28: The LORD spoke about Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor that King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon conquered. “Army of Babylon, go and attack Kedar. Lay waste those who live in the eastern desert.
NET.29: Their tents and their flocks will be taken away. Their tent curtains, equipment, and camels will be carried off. People will shout to them, ‘Terror is all around you!’”
NET.30: The LORD says, “Flee quickly, you who live in Hazor. Take up refuge in remote places. For King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon has laid out plans to attack you. He has formed his strategy on how to defeat you.”
NET.31: The LORD says, “Army of Babylon, go and attack a nation that lives in peace and security. They have no gates or walls to protect them. They live all alone.
NET.32: Their camels will be taken as plunder. Their vast herds will be taken as spoil. I will scatter to the four winds those desert peoples who cut their hair short at the temples. I will bring disaster against them from every direction,” says the LORD.
NET.33: “Hazor will become a permanent wasteland, a place where only jackals live. No one will live there. No human being will settle in it.”
NET.34: Early in the reign of King Zedekiah of Judah, the LORD spoke to the prophet Jeremiah about Elam.
NET.35: The LORD who rules over all said, “I will kill all the archers of Elam, who are the chief source of her military might.
NET.36: I will cause enemies to blow through Elam from every direction like the winds blowing in from the four quarters of heaven. I will scatter the people of Elam to the four winds. There will not be any nation where the refugees of Elam will not go.
NET.37: I will make the people of Elam terrified of their enemies, who are seeking to kill them. I will vent my fierce anger and bring disaster upon them,” says the LORD. “I will send armies chasing after them until I have completely destroyed them.
NET.38: I will establish my sovereignty over Elam. I will destroy their king and their leaders,” says the LORD.
NET.39: “Yet in days to come I will reverse Elam’s ill fortune.” says the LORD.
